original_question: Let p = 2 and G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Let A_{n,n} be the maximal elementary 2-subgroup consisting of block upper triangular matrices with identity blocks on the diagonal, so that H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n], and let det_n = det(x_{i,j}) be the degree-n class in the invariants H^n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}. If res: H^*(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n} is the restriction homomorphism, is det_n in the image of res?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Question 5.1 (Stewart Priddy): whether the determinant class det_n lies in the image of the restriction map from H^*(GL_{2n}(F_2); F_2) to H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{GL_n(F_2) x GL_n(F_2)}.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact paper target rather than a neighboring problem: it fixes p = 2, takes G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2), uses the same maximal elementary abelian subgroup A_{n,n}, identifies H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2) with a polynomial ring on generators x_{i,j}, defines det_n = det(x_{i,j}) as the degree-n invariant, and asks whether det_n is in the image of the restriction map. This is essentially the content of Question 5.1.
missing_details: State the quantifier explicitly: the question is intended for each integer n >= 1.
Define G_n := GL_n(F_2), since the invariant codomain involves G_n x G_n.
Give A_{n,n} explicitly as A_{n,n} = { [[I_n, U], [0, I_n]] : U in M_n(F_2) } inside GL_{2n}(F_2), or equivalently note that A_{n,n} is elementary abelian of rank n^2.
Specify that each x_{i,j} is a cohomology class of degree 1, so det_n is homogeneous of cohomological degree n.
Explain why the codomain is an invariant ring: N_{G_{2n}}(A_{n,n}) = G_n x G_n acts on H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2), and restriction lands in the invariants.
Make clear that the map under discussion is the degree-n part of restriction induced by the inclusion A_{n,n} -> G_{2n}.
Avoid conflating this with Question 5.2, which asks separately whether H^n(G_{2n}; F_2) is one-dimensional and generated by det_n; the paper does not present that as equivalent to Question 5.1.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 1, let G_n = GL_n(F_2) and let G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Define the maximal elementary abelian 2-subgroup A_{n,n} = { [[I_n, U], [0, I_n]] : U in M_n(F_2) } <= G_{2n}, so that H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n] with each x_{i,j} in cohomological degree 1. Since N_{G_{2n}}(A_{n,n}) = G_n x G_n, restriction along A_{n,n} -> G_{2n} lands in the invariant ring H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}. If det_n := det(x_{i,j}) in F_2[x_{i,j}] is the resulting homogeneous invariant of degree n, is det_n in the image of the degree-n restriction map H^n(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H^n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}?
justification: The paper states this problem explicitly in Section 5 as Question 5.1, after introducing A_{n,n}, the polynomial cohomology ring H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2), the normalizer N_{G_{2n}}(A_{n,n}) = G_n x G_n, the restriction map, and the class det_n. Your draft is therefore already aimed at the correct official problem. The main refinements needed are only to make the quantifier on n explicit, define G_n, specify the normalizer action that explains the invariant codomain, record that each x_{i,j} has degree 1, and say clearly that the question concerns the degree-n component of restriction. No alternate formulation is given because the next item in the paper, Question 5.2, is posed as a distinct stronger question, not as an explicit equivalent reformulation of Question 5.1.
